format.description: `guide` is hands-on instruction: it must terminate in the reader having DONE something, not merely understood it, and therefore owes at least one procedure block. It was previously unreachable -- COMPONENT_FLOOR carried a 'guide' key that no article could ever match, so guides were silently governed by the synthesis floor.

body.description: Reading-order blocks. A block is EITHER prose (p/h2/quote, which must carry text and citation_urls) OR one visual component (chart/compare/timeline/entity/scorecard/ledger/beforeafter/spectrum/flow/keyfacts/stakes/sourcecheck/stat/model/rank/counter/document, which must NOT carry a top-level text field -- wordCount() sums .text to derive the published format tier and the read-along speaks every block with .text, so a component with text would inflate the tier and read table cells aloud). Component minimums per format and the anti-fabrication rules are in agents/_shared/visual-components.md.

anyOf.description: Numbered steps the READER performs. Distinct from `flow`, which is a mechanism performed by third parties and has no success criterion. `verify` states what the reader should see; `ifnot` is the recovery branch. A step without `verify` is a claim the reader cannot check.

A copyable prompt or command. The payload is `body`, deliberately NOT `text`: a top-level text field would inflate wordCount(), promote the piece's format tier, and make the audio reader speak a template aloud. Unlike `document`, whose lines must be verbatim quotes the article already carries, a snippet is authored by the writer -- it makes no provenance claim.

A router. Every `then` must be an ACTION, not a category: 'use a bigger model' fails, 'upload it straight into a frontier chat model' passes. Distinct from `compare`, which displays difference and terminates in a cell rather than an instruction. Branches must be mutually exclusive.

Mistake, symptom, fix. Distinct from `counter`, which states the strongest case against the article's own thesis and is an editorial-integrity device. `looks` is load-bearing: a reader who cannot recognise the failure cannot apply the fix.
